newsitem.title: USA: Israel to increase Palestinian worker permits.
newsitem.headline: Israel to increase Palestinian worker permits.

text.p: Israel is to raise from 32,000 to 50,000 the number of worker permits granted to Palestinians hit by a closure of Israel's borders with the West Bank and Gaza Strip, the State Department said on Friday.

Spokesman Glyn Davies said Israeli officials announced the increase during a meeting at the State Department on Thursday of an international committee that manages the flow of aid to the self-rule Palestinian Authority.
The border closures, following a string of guerrilla attacks in Israel last February and March, have severely hit both individual Palestinians and the tax revenues of the Authority itself.
State Department officials said the increase in permits would take several weeks to implement.
But they said U.S. estimates were that if the number of permits were to rise further to 60,000, the basic revenue needs of the Authority would be met.

The officials said Thursday's meeting of a so-called ad hoc liaison committee agreed on the need to address the Authority's recurrent costs, to focus on long-term rather than short-term job creation and develop a fund-raising strategy.

A senior official who asked not to be identified said that although about 54 percent of $2.2 billion pledged in 1993 by the international community had been disbursed, there were still "significant gaps" in aid delivery.

He said the committee, meeting for the first time since right-winger Benjamin Netanyahu was elected prime minister of Israel in May, had asked the World Bank to identify those countries which had not made good on promises.

"The truth is, if we could close the gap between pledges and delivery, we would more than meet the needs that are identified both with regard to the budget and with regard to the funding of ... the core project list. That's an area where we have not done particularly well this year," he said.
The official said a budget deficit of $127 million was projected this year for the Authority, and its liquid cash requirement for the last four months of the year was about $58 million.
A full meeting of donors will be held on Nov. 18 at a European venue yet to be decided, officials said.

Representatives of Norway, the United States, Russia, Japan, Canada, the European Union, Saudi Arabia, Israel, the Palestinians, Egypt, Jordan, Tunisia, the United Nations, the World Bank and the Internationary Monetary Fund attended the Washington meeting.
